summary: Styled text for headings, paragraphs, quotes, lists and inline emphasis, as one element with a kind that picks the native tag.

kind.note: Picks the native element and the text style: h1-h4 headings, p, blockquote, list (ul around slotted li), inline-code (code), lead (p), large (div), small (small), muted (p). Heading level follows the kind; there is no separate level prop.

content.note: Default slot: the text. For kind list, slot li elements.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.notes: The native element chosen by kind (h1-h4, p, blockquote, ul, code, div, small); the default slot is its only child.

default.notes: Text or inline content. With kind list, li elements (they are projected into the inner ul and keep their list item role).

accessibility.role: Native role of the chosen element: heading (level 1-4) for h1-h4, paragraph for p, lead and muted, blockquote, list with listitem for list, code for inline-code, generic for large and small
accessibility.native: h1, h2, h3, h4, p, blockquote, ul, code, div, small
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: Content. Text elements are not named by an attribute.
aria: kind picks real semantics: h1-h4 render native headings, so the document outline is kept
list: slotted li elements stay list items of the inner ul (flattened tree)
the host adds no role; nothing is announced beyond the native element

useCases.use: kind=h1 once per page, then h2, h3, h4 in order

useCases.when: A short intro under a title
Secondary text such as hints or captions
A command, key or identifier inside a sentence

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing h3 because it looks smaller than h2
antiPatterns.why: Skipped heading levels break the outline for screen-reader users
antiPatterns.alternative: Keep levels in order and restyle with tokens

antiPatterns.why: The page has one main title

antiPatterns.pattern: Using lead, large or muted for headings
antiPatterns.why: They are not headings for assistive technology

coverage: native element per kind; h1-h4 are headings with levels
default p, kind reflects and swaps the element
size, line height and weight from component tokens per kind
inline-code and small inline, others block; inline-code in a sentence
inline-code mono on muted background; lead and muted foreground
top margin only when not the first child
h2 rule, blockquote bar and italic
slotted li stay list items with disc markers

drift.realization: Each variant is one block: flow spacing between blocks is not drawn.

openQuestions.question: One element with a variant prop, or a family of elements (sb-typography-h1 ...)?
openQuestions.recommendation: One element with variant: one stylesheet and token set, real native tags in the shadow root, same API shape as Button and Badge.
openQuestions.answer: One element, sb-typography, with variant (12 values).

openQuestions.question: Heading level separate from look (a level prop)?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: the variant picks the tag. A level prop is easy to add later if a real need appears (YAGNI).
openQuestions.answer: No level prop; h1-h4 render h1-h4.

openQuestions.question: Which reference scale do the variants follow, given the visual reference's docs now describe a newer prose system?
openQuestions.recommendation: The classic heading and prose scale, which matches the variants the owner listed.
openQuestions.answer: Follow the classic scale; the newer Typeset system is not reproduced.
